newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Restraint needed to protect coffee price-Colombian.
newsitem.headline: Restraint needed to protect coffee price-Colombian.

text.p: Coffee prices will fall if producers do not refrain from exporting part of their output, a director of Colombia's National Coffee Federation said Monday.
"If all countries export what we produce, we're going to have problems," said John Naranjo, speaking at a meeting of the CEV group of Latin American coffee producers in Quito.
Naranjo forecast 1996/97 world output of 100 million 60-kg bags. "Demand in importing countries is going to be inferior to what is going to be exported," he said.
Naranjo said that Colombia's 1995/96 production should total about 12.5 million bags. But recent heavy rains made predicting the size of next season's crop difficult.

"If the weather changes, the production is going to change but no one can be sure. The climate problem is a big variable," he said. But he added that Colombian production is not likely to hit the heights of the early 1990s, at around 18 million bags.
Naranjo said that he considered the Assocation of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to be vital for Colombia's coffee industry.

Naranjo was heading the Colombian delegation at the meeting of the CEV, which groups Central American countries, Ecuador and Venezuela. A Brazilian delegation was also present in Quito, where the Latin Americans hope to prepare common positions for upcoming meetings of the ACPC and the International Coffee Organization.
